simple.meaning: לְטָאָה (lᵉṭâʼâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a kind of lizard (from its covert habits).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לְטָאָה (H3911) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in לְטָאָה (H3911) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: לְטָאָה (lᵉṭâʼâh) / H3911 is traced through Leviticus 11:30 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a kind of lizard (from its covert habits)
definitions.full: H3911. letaah לְטָאָה noun feminine a kind of lizard (Late Hebrew id. ); — named as unclean Lev 11:30 (with תִּנְשֶׁמֶת חֹמֶט, כֹּחַ, אֲנָקָה, צָב, ), ᵐ5 χαλαβώτης , ᵑ9 stellio . — See Di on the passage Tristr Nat. Hist. Bib. 266 ff .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to hide;

occurrences.englishText: the gecko, and the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
